sermon.title: How Do We Know That We Know God?
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from John 17:1–4 that eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, that only God gives it, and that we receive it in proportion to a hearing ear. He explains how to know that we know God: the Spirit within us, keeping His commandments, being born again, and growing in the word.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the pastor names a few real people in anecdotes and examples (Muhammad, the pope, a Catholic priest by first name, and a church member “Mr. Barnes”); those names appear in the transcript only, not in the short answers or FAQs. His remarks about other religions (including the “harem” comment) and about what the pope said are given as spoken, without sources. The caption “haram” is corrected to “harem,” “tar” to “tarry,” and “meet” to “mete”; “labors” in Matthew 9:38 is shown as “laborers.” He cites “Mark 4:23” and then the words of Mark 4:24, and “Acts 4” for people speaking “in their own language.” Three spots are marked [unclear]: “one body, one [unclear]” (the caption reads “touch”), “measured, [unclear] given back” (the caption reads “meat”), and “If you [unclear] admit you’re a sinner” (the caption reads “want to”). The closing words “Rise up, son” refer to a message from the Friday night before.

chunks.section_question: What does “the hour has come” mean in John 17:1-4?
chunks.short_answer: He says John 17:1–4 is about knowing God and Jesus Christ, a very basic and powerful teaching of the Bible. He says God glorified Jesus through the virgin birth, His miracles, and mostly His death, burial and resurrection, and Jesus glorifies the Father “by reconciling people back to the father.”
chunks.text:
Now today we’re going to be talking about knowing God and Jesus Christ. This is a very very basic teaching of the Bible and very powerful. All right. Knowing— and Catholics and Protestants alike are ignoring this important doctrine. Okay. We open the book here and it’s John 17:1-4: “Father, the hour is come.” The time has come. Appointed time has come. A season has come. Okay. What time? What season? Okay. And then he explains what’s come.

“Now glorify your Son, that your Son might also glorify You.” Now God glorified Jesus by him being born of a virgin, preaching the gospel, doing miracles, bringing many into the kingdom. But mostly his death, burial, and resurrection. That’s how God honored. Glorify means honored. He honored the son with the ability to give his life. No one could take it. He had to give up his life and then he took it back again. And then how does Jesus glorify the father? By reconciling people back to the father. You see, and the time is here. We’re in that season. Jesus died on the cross. He, he went into the grave, rose again, and for the forgiveness of sin for the cleansing of sin for the freedom of sin and that we might receive him and have him living in us.

chunks.section_question: Do all religions lead to the same God? (John 17:3)
chunks.short_answer: He says John 17:3 defines eternal life as knowing “the only true God,” and “There’s only one God,” not the same God in every religion. He says the Bible explains exactly who this God is, “when you deflect from anything that he is, you got the wrong God,” and that Christians seek eternal life, not enlightenment.
chunks.text:
He gives a definition of eternal life that they may know you the only true God. The only true God. There’s only one God. And don’t give me this stuff that Buddha and Muslims and Hindus all lead to the same. No, the Bible explains exactly who this one God is. And when you deflect from anything that he is, you got the wrong God. Amen. See, we’re not looking for enlightenment. We’re looking for eternal life. The Buddhists are looking for some kind of enlightenment, an arena where they’re not reincarnated anymore. And the Muslims are looking for a harem in heaven, a— women.

That is stupid. You got God in heaven and you want a woman. I mean, how secular, how fleshly can you get? Are you with me? See, that just nullifies their God. See, now let’s take a look at these four things. We already know that Jesus has already died on the cross, rose again. Okay, God has glorified him and he has glorified the father by obeying his word and reconciling people by his blood to God. We already know that, right? That’s just basic Bible. Now you have given him authority over all flesh. Let’s check and see if historically in the scriptures this is true that Jesus Christ has authority over all mankind.

chunks.section_question: Does Jesus have authority over all flesh, and why must the Lord of the harvest be involved? (Matthew 28:18, Daniel 7:14, Matthew 9:38)
chunks.short_answer: He cites Matthew 28:18, 1 Peter 3:22 and Daniel 7:14 to say Jesus has authority over the spirit world and the earth, and is “the leader and ruler of all of them.” He cites Matthew 9:38 and says the Lord of the harvest has to be involved, using a picture of grain ground and baked into bread. He says churches that skirt the Lord of the harvest just to fill their buildings are “wasting your time,” and “We are just messengers.”
chunks.text:
Matthew 28:18: “All power is given unto me,” Jesus said, “in heaven and in earth.” In heaven is the spirit world. That’s where the angels are, the seraphims are, the demons are. Satan is. So he has authority over that whole spirit world and he has authority over the earth where humans are. Amen. And he has how much authority? All. 1 Peter 3:22: “Angels, authorities, and powers being made subject unto him.” Angels are in the spirit world. Authorities, Satan, and principalities and powers of darkness are in the spirit world. Governors and presidents and kings and so forth are in the earthly world, mayors and governors and so forth. And he is what? He is the leader and ruler of all of them.

But Daniel says it the best. Daniel 7:14: “There was given unto him dominion, glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages should—“ what? “Serve him.” He has authority over all flesh. Matthew 9:38: “Pray the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.” Jesus said, “The field is mankind.” The seed is the word of God, and the harvest is ripe, ready to be harvest. So, we need the Lord of the harvest to be involved in reaching people and harvesting them, don’t we? Yeah. It’s the Lord of the harvest that has the knowledge and the authority to plant the seed and make it grow and then cut it down and put it in the barn and then bring it out and thresh it so it to separate the stalk and the husk from the grain.

And then he puts it to the grinder and has all those kernels of grain ground into one body, one [unclear], losing their identity. And he knows how to put yeast in it, his spirit, and impregnate that, and put it in his oven, his fiery trials, so that it bakes and makes bread for the master’s table. That’s the Lord of the harvest. And you try leading people into eternal life without going through the Lord of the harvest, you’re wasting your time. You get it? He does have this power. And too many churches and too many ministers are skirting the Lord of the harvest just trying to get the churches filled. Folks, that don’t work. The Lord of the harvest has got to be involved in this.

He’s the one that can do the job. We are just messengers. Could that be true? And if we do our part and message right, he will do his part and save those that will believe. So we find that’s true. Now what authority does Jesus have to benefit mankind through his death, burial, and resurrection? See, what kind of authority does he have to benefit mankind? And he has authority over all flesh. It says in point number three that God gives people to Jesus to give them eternal life. And so I turned that around and I asked the question, how are you interested in how God’s going to do this? How does God give people to Jesus and then Jesus gives them eternal life?

chunks.section_question: What does it mean to “take heed what you hear”? (Mark 4:23-24)
chunks.short_answer: He cites Mark 4:23 on having “a hearing ear,” and says take heed means to understand, consider, apply and then experience the result. He uses a can labeled “Organic pumpkin” that opens to something that looks like tomatoes, to show that we must open things up and find out what is really inside.
chunks.text:
Have any interest in seeing the answer to that question? See, this is imperative for us. Mark 4:23: “If anyone has ears to hear, let him—“ what? “Hear.” So, we need what? A hearing ear. And then he explains what kind of hearing ear. He said to them, “Take heed what you hear.” Now that word take heed is a complex word meaning you got to understand, you got to consider it. You got to understand it, you got to apply it and then you experience the result of it. Okay? For instance, now I know you guys go to school and you’re really intelligent.

What does it say on that can? Organic pumpkin. Organic pumpkin. All right. What does it say? Organic pumpkin. So, he was right. Right. Okay. So, what are we going to find when we open this can? Pumpkin. Organic pumpkin. But how are we going to know unless we what? Apply and find out what’s really in the can. Okay, here you go. You guys know how to use a can opener? There you go. Open that can up for me. Now, guys, is that pumpkin? No. No, it’s not. No, but the can says pumpkin. It looks like salsa. It looks like tomatoes. Huh? Yeah. Is it tomatoes? Maybe. Is that a tomato? No.

He says Jesus said, “Out of your innermost being, rivers of water would flow,” a continuous flow that can cleanse us, our house and “the whole nation.”

You cannot change the word of God. Amen. See, the can doesn’t have the right stuff in it. Now, “with what measure you mete”: measure means a standard of measure. See that’s like this cup here. This is the two cup— cup. This is a teaspoon. All right. What standard of measure you meet? Which means to give out— what measure you give out is going to be measured, [unclear] given back to you. chunks.section_question: How does hearing lead to more being given? (Mark 4:24-25)
chunks.short_answer: He says “To you who hear, more will be given,” and when we respond to what God gave, He gives us more, which is how “we grow in grace.” He says whoever has not a hearing ear, even what he has “will be taken from him,” including a little faith and a little grace because they are not growing.
chunks.text:
It’s an endless supply. But then you got to put in more time to get that water. Are you there? You got to read the word and you got to understand the word. So this is how they give us eternal life. They become involved and they respond with the response that you respond back. To you who hear, more will be given. See, they that hear and then they take what God has given them. Though God gives back more than he gave them. And when they respond and give God back, he responds and gives us more. And that’s how we grow in grace and things.

For whosoever has whosoever has what? Faith, grace, a big church, a little church. No. Whosoever has ears to hear, more will be given. You see, we have to hear, understand, apply, and then we experience the results of what God said. Whosoever has not has not what? A hearing ear. Even that which he has will be taken from him.

That little bit of faith that he has will be taken away. That little bit of grace that he has will be taken away because they’re not growing in faith. They’re not growing in grace. Now, isn’t that pretty clear? And that’s how God gets involved in our life and gives us eternal life by your response. Do we really know him? This is eternal life. He says those who say “I know him” but do not keep His commandments are liars and “The truth is not in him.” He says a Christian who stumbles and gets back up is different from one who lives in habitual sin.

chunks.section_question: What does “with you” and “in you” mean, and is God three gods? (John 14:17)
chunks.short_answer: He asks who was with the apostles when Jesus said the Spirit is with you and will be in you, and says it was Jesus, who is truth, with the pouring out of the Spirit still to come. He says “Us Christians do not believe in three gods. We believe in one,” who identifies Himself as the Father, the Son, the Holy Spirit and the Word. He cites John 1:1 and John 7, rivers of life-giving water flowing from our innermost being from the Spirit, who had not come yet because Jesus had not been glorified.
chunks.text:
You know him. Hallelujah. Now, what does he mean when he says he’s talking to his apostles and he says this Holy Spirit is with you. The spirit of truth is with you, but it’s going to be in you. Now, let me answer this by asking you this question. Who was with the apostles at the time he said this? Jesus, who is truth. The Spirit is truth. You see, God says, “I’ll pour out my Spirit.” It’s God’s Spirit. You know, the Muslims say that Christianity has three gods because they use the word trinity to try to express, you know, God. But the Muslims lying.

Us Christians do not believe in three gods. We believe in one. And he identifies himself as the father, the son, the Holy Spirit, and the word. He identifies himself. So when we speak, we speak his identity. He’s the father. He’s the son. He’s the Holy Spirit. And he’s the word. Jesus said, “My word is truth.” In John 1:1, it says, “The word became flesh and dwelt amongst us. The word was with God and the word was God.” So the word is God. Jesus is God. God is God. And the Holy Spirit is God. Make no mistake, we worship one God. Can I hear an amen? Amen. Now Jesus is with them.

chunks.section_question: What is the difference between God’s presence with us and the baptism of the Holy Spirit?
chunks.short_answer: He tells of a conversation with a Catholic priest he invited to speak, who said he had been filled with the Holy Ghost at a large spirit-filled Catholic convention. He says what the priest experienced was “his presence with us,” which anyone can have when they gather and acknowledge Christ, not the baptism of the Holy Spirit. He says “That doesn’t mean your doctrine’s right.”
chunks.text:
But we also have him with us. Amen. Do you guys get this? Let me give you an illustration of this. I mingle a lot with other denominations and so especially when I was younger and I invited Father Fred, a Catholic priest in the community to come in and speak at the church. And he spoke a good message of faith and you know and in that message he said he’d been filled with the Holy Ghost. All right. And so after the service, me and him are talking, and he lights up a cigarette. And then he uses profanity like a truck driver. Blankly blanket this and blankly blanket that. And I go, “Uh, Father Fred, how did you get the Holy Ghost?” I said, “Number one, the first name of the spirit is holy.

Holy Ghost. He said, “Well, I went down to the Anaheim Convention Center where the spirit-filled Catholics gathered together.” And if you haven’t been there, it was it’s powerful. These Catholics that were filled with the spirit 1968, God just visited denominational churches and just poured out his spirit on that. He didn’t ask anybody’s permission. He just did it. And so these Catholics would get together and they’d have a a big convention. I mean, there’s 10 or 12,000 down there, man. We walk in there and they’re worshiping Jesus and all that. The power of his presence is there. But see, that’s the presence with us. And that’s what he said. I walked into that and man, the spirit of God was just came all over me and I just felt God’s presence. And I said, “Father Fred, that is not the baptism of the Holy Ghost.

That is his presence with us. Everybody can have that. When the church gets together, Jesus said, “I will be in the midst.” Presbyterians, Baptists, Methodists, Cath— I don’t care who you are. If you gather together and you acknowledge Christ, his presence will come. That doesn’t mean your doctrine’s right. I said, “Father Fred, Jesus said that the spirit would pour out of us.” I said, ‘You haven’t got the baptism of the Holy Spirit. You just experienced the first time the presence of God. And there’s a big difference. Hallelujah. And that’s what Jesus is telling his apostles. Now, there is some spirit-filled churches that believe if you don’t have the baptism of the Holy Spirit with speaking in tongues, you’re not saved and you’re going to hell.

chunks.short_answer: He says some spirit-filled churches believe if you don’t speak in tongues you’re not saved, and tells of parents who told a daughter she was going to hell for that. He says “the Bible says not all speak in tongues,” and that in Acts 2 they spoke in languages while in Acts 4 they “spoke in their own language.” He says the parents stuck with their church doctrine over Scripture because they didn’t take time to find out.

And I’m pretty sure Mr. Barnes knows who I’m talking about. And I had to— you know, I had to deal with this thing. And we all use this scripture that Jesus said, you must be born again. Unless a man is born of water and of the spirit, he can’t enter the kingdom of God. And John 1:12 says, “To as many as receive him, to them gave he power.” Now, this is God coming and dwelling with us. This is not the baptism of the Holy Ghost. He will give them power that receive him to become sons of God.

See, sons of God, when you know the interpretation of the sons of God in the Bible, the sons of God live right. They live holy. And so he empowers us to keep the word is what he’s saying. So when you invite Jesus, that initial presence of God comes. Hallelujah. And so this is what being born again is. You admit you’re a sinner. If you [unclear] admit you’re a sinner, God can’t cleanse you. He can’t forgive you. You got to admit you’re wrong. Even Christians that need areas of their life straighten out have to admit they’re wrong. That’s the formula. Hallelujah. Then after we get saved, if we seek him and we seek the word, we will grow in the word.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Jesus answered, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.
If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
But as many as received Him, to them He gave the right to become children of God, to those who believe in His name:

chunks.section_question: What is the conclusion? How do we know God?
chunks.short_answer: He says a time and season has come: Jesus has already died for the sins of the world, we must confess we are sinners and come to Him for cleansing, and “No one can save you but Jesus.” He says this is the season to possess eternal life and to know God, in proportion to our hearing ear: “You have out of God what you put into God.” He says we know God by the Spirit in us and our hearing ear to keep His word.
chunks.text:
See, desire the sincere milk of the word that you may grow by that. You’ve got to have the word to grow and you got to have the water, the spirit to grow. And unless you go to church and get in Bible studies and you’re not going to grow. So, you got to take heed what you hear. 1 Peter 1:23, born again by the word of God, which lives and abides forever. You see, we’re born again by the word of God. Remember Jesus said, “My word is spirit. The spirit is spirit. The word is spirit. All this is spirit.” All this is God’s involvement with us, folks. And he promised this is the season. You live in it. And if you’ll respond to me, I will respond to you. And if you respond more, I will respond more.

So what’s the conclusion? There’s a time and season that has come. Jesus has already died on the cross for the sins of the world. But we have to confess we are sinners and come to him for cleansing. No one can save you but Jesus. All right? And if you will admit and come to him, invite him into your life, he will back it up and he’ll come to you, forgive you, cleanse you, and live in you. He will give you eternal life. This is the season to possess eternal life. Not only to live with him forever when you die, but to know him. This is the season you can know God. And we are given these promises and other promises in proportion to our hearing ear. That’s the conclusion. You have out of God what you put into God.

That’s what Jesus said. We know. We know God by the spirit in us and our hearing ear to keep his word. We know we should be honest. We know we should be truthful. We know we should not be doing wrong. So, we know God is in us cuz he’s putting that in us. He’s compelling us. He is causing us to rise up. Rise up, son. We heard it Friday night. Rise up, son. And finish the race.

scriptures.text_nkjv: as newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that you may grow thereby,
having been born again, not of corruptible seed but incorruptible, through the word of God which lives and abides forever,

faqs.question: What does “glorify” mean in John 17?
faqs.answer: He says “Glorify means honored.” He says God honored the Son with the ability to give His life, and no one could take it.

faqs.question: What authority does he say Jesus was given before creation?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus has authority over everybody and every nation and every language on the earth: “He is the one running the kingdoms.” He says this was given to Him before creation, and He created everything.

faqs.question: Can anyone on earth give you eternal life?
faqs.answer: He says no: “There is no one on earth that can give you eternal life.” He says “Only Jesus Christ can give you eternal life.”

faqs.question: What is the difference between enlightenment and eternal life?
faqs.answer: He says “we’re not looking for enlightenment. We’re looking for eternal life.” He says eternal life is defined as knowing the only true God.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.

faqs.question: What does he say the Lord of the harvest can do?
faqs.answer: He says the Lord of the harvest has the knowledge and authority to plant the seed and make it grow, cut it down, thresh it and bake it for the master’s table. He says “He’s the one that can do the job. We are just messengers.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore pray the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into His harvest.”

faqs.question: What was the can illustration about?
faqs.answer: He opens a can labeled “Organic pumpkin” that looks like tomatoes, and says “too many of us do not dig deeper and find out if what preachers are telling us is the truth.” He says we need to put time into what we hear.

faqs.question: Who does he say gets more from God?
faqs.answer: He says it is not faith, grace, a big church or a little church: “Whosoever has ears to hear, more will be given.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For whoever has, to him more will be given; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.”

faqs.question: Is obeying God just my own effort?
faqs.answer: He says no: “It’s him providing the empowerment, the desire, the compelling to please him.” He says when he makes a mistake, that compelling picks him up and “I don’t stay in my mistake.”

faqs.question: What does he say happens when a Christian keeps messing up in an area?
faqs.answer: He says the Spirit “compels me to repent” and ask God to cleanse and free him, and he gets back up and tackles the sin again. He says one day “the spirit has given me authority over it.”

faqs.question: Are the Comforter and the Spirit of truth the same?
faqs.answer: He says “The comforter and the spirit of truth, the Holy Ghost, the Holy Spirit’s all the same thing.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him; but you know Him, for He dwells with you and will be in you.

faqs.question: Does he say Christians believe in three gods?
faqs.answer: He says no: “Us Christians do not believe in three gods. We believe in one.” He says “Make no mistake, we worship one God.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

faqs.question: How does he say we grow after we are saved?
faqs.answer: He says we “desire the sincere milk of the word that you may grow,” and you’ve got to have the word and the Spirit. He says “unless you go to church and get in Bible studies and you’re not going to grow.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: as newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that you may grow thereby,
